accuracy.evidence: Definition (cos θ, sin θ) = point at θ anticlockwise from +x on x²+y²=1; signs per quadrant (cos + in I/IV, sin + in I/II); exact values cos150 = −√3/2, sin150 = 1/2, sin210 = −1/2, cos210 = −√3/2, sin(−90) = −1, cos300 = 1/2, (0.6, −0.8) and 0.28/0.96 on the circle all checked; reference-angle and coterminal formulas checked at every parameter value by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets documented slips: cos read as the y-coordinate (swap), trig 'not existing' past 90°, carrying the reference angle's sign into other quadrants (cos150 = +√3/2, sin210 = +1/2), negative angles placed at +90°, and 1 − 0.28 instead of 1 − 0.28² in m9.

lab_distinct.evidence: Own mechanism: drag a point round x²+y²=1 with unwrapped angle (laps and clockwise negatives), live right triangle whose legs are cos and sin, reference-angle arc, quadrant signs revealed on visit, and a sin/cos graph traced only where the learner has turned. No other lab has an angle-driven circle; 0 shared shingles over the 30% limit.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learner drags to 30°, 150°, 210° and −90° and reads the signs off the coordinates before the text confirms them; the quadrant step only reveals (±,±) once each quadrant is visited; the sandbox graph is drawn by the learner's own turning, showing the period of 360° / 2π.

predictions.evidence: Five predictions, each with a tempting wrong first option the lab disproves: 'cos is the y-coordinate', 'cos150 = +√3/2', 'II has both negative', 'sin210 = +1/2', '−90° is at the top'; the reveal text names the learner's pick.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Checked in the browser for target 150°: 30° → 'Right size, wrong side… cos θ is the x-coordinate'; 330° → 'Both signs are flipped… 180° away'; 60° → 'You swapped sine and cosine'; 210° → 'Right size, wrong height… sin θ is the y-coordinate'; 100° → coordinates plus move left/down.

readability.evidence: FK grade kid 1.4 (limit 6.5) and adult 6.0 (limit 9.5); one idea per paragraph, every claim tied to a concrete angle (150°, 210°); the adult text ends with the named common mistakes.

no_filler.evidence: Every sentence states a definition, a sign rule, a worked value or a slip; content gate finds no filler phrases and no explanation overlap above 12% with any other lesson; feedback messages quote the learner's own coordinates.

mobile.evidence: iPhone 13 screenshots: circle stacked above the graph, coordinate/cos/sin pills readable and not clipped, the sin pill moves under the axis when the leg is short, turn buttons wrap two rows; real CDP touch drags hit 30°, 150°, −90° and every challenge angle; no element wider than the viewport.

accessibility.evidence: Every task doable with ±1°/±15° buttons (step 4 completed by buttons only in the walkthrough); Radians and Show whole curves are aria-pressed toggles; canvas aria-label and the live description give θ, both coordinates with exact surds, quadrant and reference angle; reduced motion removes the pulse and glides; axe clean in both themes.
